Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from this washed-out 1st T20I. The second game of the series will be played on Saturday, 14th June at 2 pm GMT. But as you know, you can always join us early for all the build-up for the match. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

Hang on! The umpires walk straight up to the dressing rooms, and there it is - the handshakes are done. THE MATCH IS OFFICIALLY ABANDONED. The rain gods have had their say, and the spoils will be shared. Disappointing, yes, but the weather is out of anyone’s hands. West Indies get a bit more rest before the second game as they just played a T20I series against England, while Ireland will be fired up to put on a strong performance at home.

UPDATE - 2.52 pm GMT - The covers remain firmly in place as the rain continues to fall steadily. This is not an encouraging sign, indicating a lengthy delay ahead. Even if the rain stops now, the groundstaff would still require a minimum of 90 minutes to clear the water and prepare the field for play. The match officials, including the umpires, have been out for an inspection under their umbrellas but have since returned after a brief discussion. An official update is expected shortly!

UPDATE - 2.23 pm GMT - Well, nothing new to update about as the visuals look pretty gloomy. It is currently drizzling, but the covers remain firmly on, and all we can do is wait and hope for the conditions to get better.

While we wait for this match to start, just beside us in England at Lord's, the World Test Championship Final between Australia and South Africa is unfolding with gripping intensity. The Aussies have seized a significant advantage, establishing a 74-run lead after bundling out South Africa for a paltry 138 in the second inning, replying to Australia’s challenging first-inning total of 212. Spearheading this dominance has been the Australian skipper, Pat Cummins, who delivered a masterclass in seam bowling, claiming a scintillating five-wicket haul and once again exemplifying his ability to lead from the front on the grandest stage. With both sides having completed an innings apiece, the final hangs finely balanced, yet tilting towards Australia. The surface has offered ample assistance to the bowlers, with variable bounce and persistent seam movement creating a stern examination for the batters. As Australia now looks to consolidate their lead, the looming question remains - how formidable will the target be for South Africa in the fourth inning under such treacherous conditions? Hence, to find out, you can just switch tabs to see our coverage of that match!

As per the reports, there has been significant rain around Bready, and the outfield has taken a lot of water. It is still raining, and the covers are firmly on, and even if the rain stops, it will take a lot of time for the grounds staff to prepare the ground. However, we can be hopeful of getting some action, but for now, the toss and start of the match are officially delayed.

All in all, we are set up for what promises to be a thrilling contest between two sides hungry to assert themselves. Both teams are dealing with transitions, new faces, and plenty of motivation to make their mark early in this vital T20I series. The conditions at Bready are expected to offer something for both batters and bowlers, making the contest even more intriguing. The stage is set, the stakes are high - who will seize the early advantage? Stay tuned for the toss and playing XI!

On the flip side, Ireland have quietly built a very competitive and spirited unit over the years. They are no longer the underdogs who show up occasionally, as they’ve developed a knack for producing match-winners capable of toppling even the strongest teams on their day. One of their brightest stars is the talented Harry Tector, who has grown into a reliable batter with a calm head and the ability to pace his innings according to the situation. Their bowling unit, once seen as their weak link, has made significant strides lately. Pacers bring consistency, while their spinners have become adept at controlling the middle overs, especially on slower surfaces. With their eyes firmly set on assembling a rock-solid core for the upcoming T20 World Cup, this series offers a golden opportunity to test bench strength.

The West Indies come into this T20I series carrying a mixed bag of form, as their confidence took a serious dent after suffering a whitewash in the T20I series against England, which has left plenty of questions for their coaching staff and selectors. However, they did manage to find a few bright spots in the preceding ODI series, where Keacy Carty emerged as a shining light, hammering back-to-back centuries and showcasing his immense talent. His performances have injected some stability into the Windies' fragile batting lineup. Also, the Cricket West Indies Board needs to carefully recalibrate their player management strategies. That said, their bowling department remains rich with experience, thanks to several of their pacers and spinners sharpening their skills in global T20 leagues. With the next World Cup looming in less than eight months, this series will serve as a crucial audition for many players vying to cement their spots in the squad.

Hello and welcome to the opening clash of the 3-match T20I series between West Indies and Ireland, coming to you from the picturesque Bready Cricket Club. These two sides recently locked horns in a 3-match ODI series just last month, where both managed to snatch a win each, while one encounter was lost to rain. Now, they shift focus to the shortest and most electrifying format of the game - T20 cricket. The last time these teams faced each other in this format was back in the T20 World Cup 2022, where Ireland stunned the Windies with a clinical and comfortable victory in the group stage. With the T20 World Cup 2026 slowly approaching on the horizon, this series holds crucial significance for both teams to fine-tune their squads, experiment with combinations, and discover players who can thrive on the big stage.

Cricket never takes a breather these days, and honestly, we’re not complaining. Now, let’s talk about the West Indies for a moment. When these guys step onto the field, you know you’re about to witness something extraordinary. There’s this undeniable charisma they bring – call it Caribbean magic or just pure entertainment value – but whatever it is, it works. Even the harshest critics find themselves secretly rooting for those moments of brilliance that the Windies can deliver. Of course, results have been disappointing for the Men in Maroon as they have managed only single match on this Irish-English tour, in fact, out of ten matches played across all there formats, the Windies have won just two - a famous Test match win in Multan back in January, and defeating Ireland last month in the third ODI, which saved them from a series defeat. But, they’re a group looking for resurrection. These men have been putting in some serious miles lately. They’ve been on the road for over a month with an ODI series in Ireland, then packed their bags for England, where they battled through multiple white-ball formats. And now? They’ve come full circle, landing back in Ireland for what promises to be an electric three-match T20I series. After a series draw in ODIs, is a comeback on cards? But here’s the shocker, and quite an unexpected one. Considered as their bright future prospect in limited overs, Nicholas Pooran has announced retirement from international cricket at just 29 years old. Pooran, though, didn’t feature lately, but still it has left a huge void in their batting. Shai Hope steps up to captain this 14-man squad with Sherfane Rutherford as his deputy. Hope has been finding his rhythm throughout this tour, consistently getting among the runs, while Rutherford comes in riding high on confidence after a brilliant IPL campaign where his bat did most of the talking. The real buzz though, surrounds young Keacy Carty, who’s been making waves with some seriously impressive knocks at the top of the order. If he can keep this momentum going, the Windies might just have found their next big thing. A new name in the batting department, Jyd Goolie, is all set to represent the Maroons and will be interesting to watch. Opening duties fall to Evin Lewis and Johnson Charles, both eager to make their mark and set the tone from ball one. The middle order looks solid with Shimron Hetmyer and Rovman Powell ready to unleash some serious power hitting when the situation demands. The all-round strength comes from Jason Holder and Romario Shepherd, two players who can change the game with both bat and ball. On the bowling front, the pace attack revolves around Matthew Forde and Alzarri Joseph, while the spin department is in the capable hands of Akeal Hosein and Gudakesh Motie. It’s a well-balanced unit that has all the tools to make this series memorable. Ireland have had their own ups and downs in the last year or two. However, they had a rocking start to the ODI series a month back. But, they have certainly lost some fire power in all departments with the likes of Curtis Campher, Gareth Delany, and Craig Young withdrawing their names from this series. Paul Stirling will continue to lead the side and they still have the likes of Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker, Mark Adair, and George Dockrell as their experienced core, rounding up all three departments. Despite the absence of Young, the pace trio of Josh Little and the two McCarthys, they look potent. While Ben White, Matthew Humphreys and Gavin Hoey are their spin resources. The series is scheduled to be played at Bready Cricket Club as an exclusive venue and an interesting T20I series is up next. Last 5 matches see them level at 2-2, with one turning into a no result. So as the Windies gear up for this final leg of their Irish adventure, one thing’s for certain, we’re in for a treat. T20I cricket, Caribbean flair, and a hungry Irish side looking to make their mark – what more could you ask for?
